summary: No fundamentals-based thesis broke today. Close.json holds no filing or screen evidence against DPZ, IDXX, WMT, FAST, CARG, KR, MSCI, VRSN or MSM. Their invalidations rest on price stops, a guidance cut or cfo falling below net income, and none of those is documented in the files today. The one tripped invalidation, BTC/USD, was a price rule on a non-fundamental asset and was sold in full, so it is outside my remit. Open items: DPZ's guidance-cut report is still unconfirmed, and the DPZ, MSCI, FAST and MSM sector labels are unreliable. WMT (11-19) and KR (12-03) have earnings ahead, and the screen data is annual and will not show those prints.
update: Stored theses carry no stale fundamentals claims that need correcting, apart from the label caveats. DPZ's Staples rank is a wholesale-groceries SIC artifact, so its case rests on absolute quality (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M), and the stored thesis already says so. MSCI is labelled Industrials, not Financials. WMT, DPZ and KR still count as about 26% Staples by label (L3), and I am not suggesting adds. Today's moves are not evidence against any thesis: IDXX +4.5%, FAST +3.0%, CARG +2.4% and MSM +5.3% were all up, and KR -0.7% and VRSN -0.9% were small down days. The VNQ buy is an ETF and has no fundamentals thesis to grade. I did not re-read inputs/fundamentals.json for this review. Watch next: the WMT print on 11-19 against its guidance-cut clause, the KR print on 12-03, and any filing that confirms or refutes DPZ's guidance cut.
